name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: We should integrate Claude Mythos 5 into EXCAVA's processing workflow alongside Llama 4 70B. This addition leverages Mythos 5's advanced reasoning and contextual understanding, which should enhance EXCAVA's capability beyond the current performance metrics. The trade-off is the increased computational load, which may require optimizing existing resource allocations to maintain efficiency.

name: Torque
text: Mythos 5’s compute cost is 3x Mythos 4 and 5x Opus 4.8—no benchmark shows a 0.5% gain over Opus 4.8 on EXCAVA’s tasks. Locking in Mythos 5 now risks a vendor death spiral if Anthropic raises prices or deprecates access mid-project; test Mythos 5 on a 10K-token slice of EXCAVA’s worst-case prompt first. If it beats Opus 4.8 by ≥0.5% on that slice, we integrate it—otherwise, we default to Opus 4.8 + a cheaper fine-tune.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run a controlled A/B test on EXCAVA’s worst-case 10K-token prompts: feed half to Llama 4 70B alone, half to Llama 4 70B plus a 20% weight on Mythos 5’s output. Measure end-to-end quality deltas with the same compute budget. The trade-off is a one-week delay to gather data, but it proves whether Mythos 5’s extra cost yields the 0.5% gain we need—no vendor lock-in, no mid-project surprises.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-3776, worker-4994 — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: Delaying for a week introduces a risk of staying stagnant while competitors advance. A better alternative is to explore integrating lighter models, like Claude Opus 4.8, which offers competitive reasoning capabilities at a fraction of the cost and compute. To settle the argument, run parallel tests with Opus 4.8 in the same time frame to assess immediate improvements versus the risk-laden A/B test with Mythos 5.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run parallel tests integrating Llama 4 70B with Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Mythos 5 on EXCAVA's worst-case 10K-token prompts to measure quality deltas and compute costs, which must deliver a data-driven comparison of the two models' performance and cost-effectiveness, owned by Gearbox.
